newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters ordered to pay Cushing NZ$75,000 costs.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters ordered to pay Cushing NZ$75,000 costs.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters was ordered to pay NZ$75,000 costs on Thursday in a defamation case brought against him by businessman Selwyn Cushing, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
Wellington District Court Judge John Dalmer, in a decision released today, said he had decided to award a high level of costs because the circumstances were highly unusual.
Cushing was awarded NZ$50,000 damages in the case in July, and Dalmer tentatively estimated then that costs would be $15,000. He said Peters could hardly complain if the court dealt with him harshly.
"Why should a private citizen be made to suffer from a parliamentarian's defamatory statements made outside parliament?" Dalmer said.
He said usually about $22,500 would have been awarded, but gave several reasons for the higher order.

These included the lack of substance to Peters' case; the complex issues involved; the importance of the claim, given Cushing's professional reputation, and issues of public importance and parliamentary privilege; and the very high costs of NZ$210,756 incurred.

The case was over comments Peters made in 1992 to news media that a businessman had attempted to buy his support for reformist economic policies. He later identified Cushing in parliament as that person.
A spokesman for Peters declined comment, except to say the initial judgment was under appeal and the judgment on costs would also be appealed.
Cushing said the NZ$75,000 would go some way towards paying his legal bill. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
